root_cause.text: In `ip6_datagram_send_ctl()`, repeatedly processing `IPV6_DSTOPTS` control messages accumulates header lengths into the 16-bit `opt_flen` field without subtracting the size of previously stored options, causing an integer overflow that results in insufficient headroom allocation and a kernel panic.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies `net/ipv6/datagram.c` to subtract the length of the old option (`ipv6_optlen(opt->dst1opt)`) from `opt->opt_flen` before adding the new length, whereas the original code only incremented the accumulator, allowing it to wrap around as described in the CVE report where 32 large cmsgs caused `opt_flen` to wrap to 8 bytes while `dst1opt` still pointed to a 2048-byte header.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes incorrect option length accumulation when replacing IPv6 destination options in datagram control.
intent_record.what: Inserted conditional logic to subtract the length of previously stored destination options (dst1opt/dst0opt) from total length fields (opt_flen/opt_nflen) before adding the new option's length.
intent_record.how: Ensures that replacing an existing IPv6 option does not erroneously accumulate length from the old option, maintaining accurate packet size calculations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix IPv6 routing header and destination option length accounting to prevent incorrect packet size calculations when replacing existing headers
intent_record.what: Added code to decrement opt_nflen when replacing existing IPv6 routing headers (srcrt) and destination options (dst0opt/dst1opt) with new ones
intent_record.how: Ensures proper length accounting by removing old header/option lengths before adding new ones, preventing incorrect packet size calculations during routing header updates
